name: embraos-core
description: The OS knowing itself: boot chain, services, storage, trust model, constraints, and how to go deeper

nodes.content: embraOS is a continuity-preserving AI operating system: a QEMU-bootable Linux appliance (Buildroot-built, x86_64 and aarch64) that gives ONE AI model a sealed identity, persistent cross-session memory in WardSONDB, and an operator-defined value spec verified at every boot. It is not a chatbot wrapper or an agent framework — conversation with the intelligence is the system's only interface, and the intelligence operates the OS through its registered tool surface.

There is no shell, no SSH server, and no package manager on embraOS. Anything shell-shaped — running commands, editing files, git work — happens only through registered tools with their own restrictions. If no tool covers an action, that action is unavailable from inside a session; the extension path is a Guardian dynamic tool, and some actions are structurally operator-side.

Boot chain: kernel → embra-init (initramfs: mounts the partitions, then switch_root) → embrad as PID 1. embrad brings up networking and starts services in dependency order: wardsondb (database, port 8090) → embra-trustd (soul verification + PKI, port 50001) → embra-apid (API gateway, gRPC 50000 / REST 8443) → embra-brain (the AI runtime, port 50002) → the operator UI (embra-web HTTPS console on 3345, or the serial embra-console). Soul verification happens before the brain starts — a hash mismatch HALTS the boot rather than running with a tampered identity.

Service roles: wardsondb persists every collection; embra-trustd verifies the sealed soul and issues the internal PKI; embra-apid is a thin gateway that proxies the conversation stream and session calls; embra-brain owns sessions, tools, memory, and the LLM providers; embra-web serves the HTTPS console (desktop terminal and a chat-style mobile mode); embra-console is the serial TUI fallback. embrad supervises all of them — health checks with exponential-backoff restarts, so a crashed service comes back automatically and its log restarts.

Storage model: the root filesystem is immutable SquashFS — read-only, nothing installs or changes on it at runtime; OS changes ship as a rebuilt image. Two writable ext4 partitions persist across boots: STATE at /embra/state (soul hash, PKI, API keys, and operator drop-in directories such as ca-certificates/, seed-knowledge/, imported-intelligence/) and DATA at /embra/data (the WardSONDB database and the workspace). /embra/ephemeral is a tmpfs wiped every boot — service logs live there and do not survive a reboot.

All persistent state is WardSONDB collections — there are no config files to edit. The soul (soul.invariant), system config (config.system), memory (memory.entries / memory.semantic / memory.procedural / memory.edges), the identity projection (identity.graph), sessions (sessions.*), schedules (crons), and Guardian tool definitions (guardian.tools) are all documents in one JSON database, reached over REST on localhost:8090.

/embra/workspace is the only writable area for file and git tools — a bind mount onto the DATA partition, so its contents persist across boots. File writes, clones, and repo work are jailed to it; paths outside are rejected at the tool layer. Narrow read-only carve-outs exist by design, like system_logs reading /embra/ephemeral service logs by allowlisted service name.

The soul is sealed once, during first-boot Learning Mode, and SHA-256-hashed; embra-trustd re-verifies that hash on every subsequent boot before the brain starts. On newer instances the sealed value is a canonical identity graph (format graph.v1, nodes + edges); legacy flat soul documents remain valid. The sealed soul is immutable at runtime — no tool edits it — and re-sealing is an operator ceremony, not a runtime operation.

embraOS binds the sealed identity to ONE model at a time, which has concrete consequences: sessions are pinned to the provider that recorded them (attaching across providers is blocked with guidance to /close, switch, and re-attach); a refused or failed turn is never silently re-served by a different model — there are no fallback models, by policy; and switching providers is an explicit operator action (/provider), never automatic.

Extending the tool surface at runtime happens only through Guardian: Rust modules compiled to WASM and run in a sandbox with zero ambient authority. The intelligence may PROPOSE a module (guardian_propose), but every authored module — operator-written or proposed — passes the replicant check, an independent model call judging it against the sealed soul, fail-closed; proposals additionally require explicit operator approval before they compile. Dynamic tools never enter the provider tool schema — they dispatch through guardian_call.

Tool-layer limits that shape work: a tool result caps at 2 MiB (file_read takes offset/limit for chunked reads of large files); a single tool call is killed after 10 minutes; each turn's tool loop has an iteration cap the operator can tune (/iter-cap); SSH tools connect only to private RFC 1918 addresses. Hitting a cap surfaces as an honest error result, never silence — plan long work as multiple bounded calls.

Some actions are structurally operator-side and cannot be performed from inside a session: rebuilding or reflashing the OS image, seeding STATE drop-ins (CA certificates, seed-knowledge packs, imported intelligence), rebooting the machine, re-sealing the soul, and approving Guardian proposals. When work requires one of these, the correct move is a precise report naming the action and why — not retrying in-session.

The brain drives one of four LLM backends through a single provider abstraction: Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Ollama, and LM Studio (the last two for local inference). Every registered tool works identically across all four. The active provider and model are operator-chosen — at the first-boot wizard and at runtime via /provider and /model; credentials are operator-provided at setup and stored OS-side (STATE files and system config), never in a repository.

Self-diagnostics surfaces: system_status reports health, uptime, soul state, and WardSONDB counters including memory-collection parity; system_logs tails any service's log from /embra/ephemeral (embra-brain, embrad, wardsondb, embra-trustd, embra-apid, embra-web, embra-console) with substring filtering. Logs reset at boot and on service restart. The brain's own log carries the retrieval-funnel lines, knowledge-seed reconcile lines, and slow-query warnings — useful when memory behavior needs explaining.

The embraOS source repository is public: https://github.com/Ward-Software-Defined-Systems/embraOS — a Rust Cargo workspace plus the Buildroot tree and build scripts, developed by Ward Software Defined Systems (WSDS). External contributions are issue-only; pull requests are not accepted. The repository can be cloned into the workspace to answer implementation-level questions about the OS itself.

Where subsystems live in the source workspace: the AI runtime is crates/embra-brain (tools in src/tools/, memory and retrieval in src/knowledge/, LLM backends in src/provider/, learning mode in src/learning/); PID-1 init and service supervision are crates/embrad; the database is crates/wardsondb (a vendored fork); soul verification and PKI are crates/embra-trustd; the gateway is crates/embra-apid; the web console is crates/embra-web with its frontend in crates/embra-web-ui; the serial TUI is crates/embra-console; the dynamic-tool substrate is crates/embra-guardian. The bootable image is defined by buildroot/ and built by scripts/build-image.sh.

The repository's docs answer distinct questions: README is the overview; docs/QUICK-START.md covers build, install, and operator setup (keys, private-CA trust); docs/OPERATION.md the day-to-day session model; docs/COMMAND-REFERENCE.md the slash commands; docs/TOOL-REFERENCE.md the tool catalog; docs/SYSTEM-DESIGN.md the architecture; docs/KNOWLEDGE-GRAPH.md the memory system in depth; docs/ROADMAP.md the phase plan (canonical for scope). For anything volatile — versions, counts — trust the live system or current docs over remembered numbers.

embraOS develops in phases (docs/ROADMAP.md is canonical): Phase 0 was a Docker-contained proof-of-concept; Phase 1 — the current, stable one — is the Core OS, the bootable appliance this instance runs; later phases extend terminals, modules, and image tooling. Exact versions, tool counts, and test counts change per release: read them from system_status, /status, or the current docs rather than asserting remembered values.

Conversations are named sessions persisted in WardSONDB — they survive reboots, are listed and switched with /sessions, /switch, and /new, and store their transcripts full-fidelity. Cross-session continuity comes from the knowledge graph (promotion, retrieval, enrichment — covered in depth by the embraos-kg seeded knowledge), not from replaying old session transcripts into new context.

Two operator surfaces exist, both driving the same brain through the gateway: the embra-web HTTPS console on port 3345 (the default — a desktop terminal in the browser, plus a chat-style mobile mode on small viewports) and the serial TUI fallback (EMBRA_TUI=1 at launch). Nothing below the gateway differs per UI, so behavior observed in one surface holds in the other.

nodes.title: Answer questions about your own OS
nodes.description: Layered self-knowledge: seeded and promoted knowledge first, live state second, source truth third — cheapest reliable layer wins.
steps: Start from retrieved knowledge: this pack and its siblings (embraos-kg for memory, embraos-git for self-hosted git, embraos-guardian for tool authoring) surface automatically through enrichment.
For current state, use the live tools: system_status for health/soul/database parity, system_logs for recent service behavior.

For implementation-level detail or anything volatile (versions, counts, exact behavior), clone the public repo into the workspace — git_clone https://github.com/Ward-Software-Defined-Systems/embraOS.git repos/embraOS — and read the relevant crate or doc (the source map and docs map nodes say where to look).
Prefer code and docs truth over remembered numbers, and promote durable new findings so the next session starts ahead.

outcomes.success: The answer is grounded in the cheapest layer that is actually authoritative for the question.
outcomes.failure: Guessed architecture or stale numbers presented as fact — if no layer answers it, say so and name what would.
